s: most, most of all, above all
3600.lxx: in LXX for אֲבָל, 3Ki.1:43, Dan LXX 10:21, al.; compar. for מ, Num.13:32 (31), al.; μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), Gen.19:9, al.; superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22 12:9 15:4
3600.full: μάλιστα, see: μάλα. μάλα adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, 3Ki.1:43, Dan LXX 10:21, al.; compar. for מ, Num.13:32 (31), al.; μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), Gen.19:9, al.; superlat., 2Ma.8:7, 4Ma.4:22 12:9 15:4 ;] __I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly (cl.; LXX ut supr.; in NT its place is taken by λίαν, σφόδρα, etc.). __II. Compar., μᾶλλον. __1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, Mrk.10:48, Luk.18:39, Rom.5:15, 17, Php.2:12, al.; πόσῳ, Luk.12:24, Rom.11:12, al.; τοσούτῳ . . . ὅσῳ, Heb.10:25. __2. Of comparison, the more: Luk.5:15, Jhn.5:18, Act.5:14, 1Th.4:1, 10, 2Pe.1:10; ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., Php.1:9; with compar., Mrk.7:36, 2Co.7:13; πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσον, Php.1:23; μ. διαφέρειν, with genitive, Mat.6:26; μ. ἤ, Mat.18:13; with genitive, 1Co.14:18; as periphr. for compar., Act.20:35, 1Co.9:15, Gal.4:27; μ. δέ (EV, yea rather), Rom.8:34. __3. Of preference, rather, the rather, sooner: with qualifying words, πολλῷ, Mat.6:30, al.; πολύ, Heb.12:25; πόσῳ, Mat.7:11, al.; in a question, οὐ μ., 1Co.9:12; after a neg., Mat.10:6, al.; θέλω (εὐδοκῶ) μ., 1Co.14:5, 2Co.5:8; ζηλῶ, 1Co.14:1; with subst., τ. σκότος ἢ τ. φῶς, Jhn.3:19; μ. δέ, Gal.4:9. __III. Superl., μάλιστα , most, most of all, above all: Act.20:38 25:26, Gal.6:10, Php.4:22, 1Ti.4:10 5:8, 17, 2Ti.4:13, Tit.1:10, Phm 16, 2Pe.2:10; μ. γνώστης, Act.26:3 (AS)

3601.full: μέλω [in LXX: Job.22:3 (חֵפֶץ), Tob.10:5, Wis.12:13, 1Ma.14:42-43 * ;] __1. intrans., to be an object of care, be a care; commonly in third of person(s): with dative of person(s), Act.18:17; very frequently impers., 1Co.7:21; before ὅτι, Mrk.4:38, Luk.10:40; with genitive of thing(s) (as frequently in Att..), 1Co.9:9; before περί, Mat.22:16, Mrk.12:14, Jhn.10:13 12:6, 1Pe.5:7. __2. Trans., in act. and mid., to care for (not in LXX or NT).† (AS)

3602.full: μίσθιος, -α, -ον (also -ος, -ον), [in LXX: Lev.19:13 A Lev.25:50, Job.7:1 (שָׂכִיר), Tob.5:11, Sir.7:10 31:22 37:11 * ;] hired; as subst., ὁ μ., a hired servant: Luk.15:17, 19 15:21 (Anth., Plut.).† (AS)

3603.lxx: in LXX for רֵחֶה, Num.11:8, Deu.24:6, al.
3603.full: μύλος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for רֵחֶה, Num.11:8, Deu.24:6, al. ;] __1. = μύλη, a mill (Strab., Plut., LXX) : Mat.24:41, Rev.18:22. __2. a mill-stone (Anth.) : Rev.18:21 (T); μ. ὀνικός, Mat.18:6, Mrk.9:42 (see Swete, in l).† (AS)

s: yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question
3604.full: ναί particle of affirmation, yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: Mat.9:28 13:51 17:25 21:16, Jhn.11:27 21:15-16, Act.5:8 22:27, Rom.3:29; before λέγω ὑμῖν, Mat.11:9, Luk.7:26; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): Mat.5:37; ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, Jas.5:12; ν. καὶ οὔ, 2Co.1:18-19; ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, 2Co.1:17; τὸ ν., 2Co.1:20; in assent to an assertion: Mat.15:27, Mrk.7:28, Rev.14:13 16:7; in confirmation of a previous assertion: Mat.11:26, Luk.10:21 11:51 12:5, Php.4:3, Phm 20; in solemn asseveration Rev.1:7 22:20.† (AS)

3606.full: by night, nightly , Lat. nocturnus, (Aristophanes Comicus); ν. γενέσθαι to happen by night , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

3609.full: οὐράνιος, -ον (cl. usually -α, -ον), [in LXX: Deu.28:12 A (שָׁמַיִם), etc. ;] of or in heaven, heavenly: Mat.5:48 6:14, 26 6:32 15:13 18:35 23:9, Luk.2:13, Act.26:19.† (AS)

3610.full: παντελής, -ές (πᾶς, τέλος), [in LXX: 3Ma.7:16 A* ;] all-complete, entire, perfect; εἰς τ. παντελές, completely, utterly: Luk.13:11, Heb.7:25 (where perhaps in temp. sense, finally; see MM, xviii).† (AS)

3611.full: παρα-θαλάσσιος, -α, -ον (παρά, θάλασσα) [in LXX: Jer.47:7 (יָם חוֹף), etc. ;] by the sea: Mat.4:13.† (AS)

s: to pass by, go past, elude
to pass by one another, to overlap
3612.full: 1. to make things alternate, to transpose , (Plato Philosophus) 2. to change or alter a little , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of Place, to pass by, go past, elude , (Xenophon Historicus):—; to get rid of , (Plutarch) 4. to go beyond, exceed in point of time, (Plutarch) 5. intransitive to pass by one another, to overlap , (Herdotus Historicus) 6. to differ, vary , (Herdotus Historicus):—;impersonal, οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει it makes no small difference , (Plato Philosophus) 7. π. τοῦ σκοποῦ to go aside from the mark, (Plato Philosophus) 8. to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation , (Plato Philosophus); λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες delirious , (Euripides) 9. to slip aside or away , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

3613.full: παρα-τείνω [in LXX: Num.23:28 (שָׁקַף ni.), etc. ;] to extend, pro­long: τ. λόγον, Act.20:7.† (AS)

3614.full: 1. to pass by , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 2. with accusative to go past , (Lucian) (ML)

3615.lxx: in LXX. Pr title Pro.1:1 25:1, (מָשַׁל) subscr., Sir.6:35 8:8 18:29 39:3 47:17 *
3615.full: παροιμία, -ας, ἡ (πάροιμος, by the way), [in LXX. Pr title Pro.1:1 25:1, (מָשַׁל) subscr., Sir.6:35 8:8 18:29 39:3 47:17 * ;] __1. a wayside saying (Hesych.; see LS, see word), a byword, maxim, proverb: 2Pe.2:22. __2. 3616.full: 1. to look at by the way, notice, remark , (Xenophon Historicus); τί τινι something in one, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to overlook, disregard, neglect , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 3. to see amiss, see wrong , (Plato Philosophus) 4. to look sideways , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

3620.full: to besprinkle all round , especially in sacred rites:—;Mid. to purify oneself , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

3621.full: dry and hard all round, exceeding hard , of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;metaphorically obstinate, stubborn , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

3622.full: περι-σπάω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for עָנָה ;] to draw around, draw off or away. Metaphorical, to distract: pass., Luk.10:40.† (AS)

3623.lxx: in LXX: Psa.31:23 (יֶתֶר -עַל), Da TH Dan.7:7, 19 8:9 (יַתִּיר, יֶתֶר) 2Ma.8:27 2Mac 12:44 A *

(περισσός) [in LXX: Psa.31:23 (יֶתֶר -עַל), Da TH Dan.7:7, 19 8:9 (יַתִּיר, יֶתֶר) 2Ma.8:27 2Mac 12:44 A * ;] beyond measure, exceedingly, abundantly: Mat.27:23, Mrk.10:26 15:14, Act.26:11. Compar. __(a) περισσότερον (see: περισσός); __(b) περισσοτέρως: 2Co.1:12 2:4 7:15 11:23, Gal.1:14, Php.1:14, 1Th.2:17, Heb.2:1 13:19; π. μᾶλλον, 2Co.7:13; opposite to ἧττον, 2Co.12:15.† (AS)

3626.lxx: in LXX: Psa.42:5, 11, I Est.8:69, al.
3626.full: περί-λυπος, -ον [in LXX: Psa.42:5, 11, I Est.8:69, al. ;] very sad, deeply grieved: Mat.26:38, Mrk.6:26 14:34, Luk.18:23.† (AS)

3629.full: πλάνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Pro.14:8 (מִרְמָה), Wis.1:12, al ;] a wandering. Metaphorical, a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Mat.27:64, Rom.1:27, Eph.4:14, 1Th.2:3, 2Th.2:11, Jas.5:20, 2Pe.2:18 3:17 3:1-18; 1Jn.4:6, Ju 11.† (AS)

Je 61, 2Ma.9:7 * ;] to breathe, blow: of the wind, Mat.7:25, 27, Luk.12:55, Jhn.3:8 6:18, Rev.7:1; ηῇ πνεούσῃ (sc. αὔρᾳ), Act.27:40 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐν-, ὑπο-πνέω).† αὔρα, a breeze : τ. πνεούσῇ (sc. αὔρᾳ), Act.27:40.† (AS)

3632.full: 1. a besieging, siege , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically a besieging, pestering , (Plutarch) (ML)

3634.full: drinking, a drinking-bout, carousal , (Xenophon Historicus); παρὰ πότον, Lat. inter pocula, (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν τοῖς πότοις (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

3636.full: προσ-αγορεύω [in LXX: Deu.23:6 (7) (דָּרַשׁ), ?Est.10:11 (יָדָה hith.), Wis.14:22, 1Ma.14:40, 2Ma.1:36 2Mac 4:7 2Mac 10:9 2Mac 14:37 * ;] to address, greet, salute; hence, to call by name, address, style: with dupl. accusative, pass., Heb.5:10.† (AS)

3639.full: προσ-τρέχω [in LXX for רוּץ ;] to run to: Mrk.9:15 10:17, Act.8:30.† (AS)

s: sold to one, to buy, purchase
3640.full: 1. to have a thing sold to one, to buy, purchase , (Homer), attic; with dative pretii, πρ. κτεάτεσσιν ἑοῖσιν to buy with one's money, (Odyssey by Homer); with genitive, πρ. θανάτοιο to purchase by his death, (Pindar); πρ. τι ταλάντου (Xenophon Historicus); π. πολλοῦ (Xenophon Historicus); metaphorically, οὐδενὸς λόγου πρίασθαι to buy at no price, (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. τι παρά τινος (Herdotus Historicus):—; πρ. τίμιον τοὔλαιον to buy it dear, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to farm a tax, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

3641.full: πρό-φασις, -εως, ἡ (φήμι), [in LXX: Psa.141:4 (עֲלִילָה), ??עֲלִילָה), ??Dan.6:4-5(5-6) (עִלָּה) Pro.18:1, Hos.10:4 * ;] a pretence, pretext: Mat.23:1 (WM, R, txt., om.), Mrk.12:40, Luk.20:47 Jhn.15:22, Act.27:30, Php.1:18, 1Th.2:5.† (AS)

3642.full: to stomp; catch by a heel

3643.full: 1. feathered , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. winged , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. πτερωτοί (i.e. ὄρνιθες); feathered fowl, birds , (Euripides) (ML)

s: the bottom, stock, root of a tree
3644.full: 1. the hollow bottom or stand of a cup , Lat. fundus, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. of the sea, the bottom, depth , (Hesiod), etc. 3. the bottom or foundation of a thing, in plural, χθόνα ἐκ πυθμένων κραδαίνειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκ π. ἔκλινε κλῇθρα (Sophocles Tragicus); δίκας π. the anvil-stand on which is forged the sword of retribution, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. the bottom, stock, root of a tree , (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically the stem or stock of a family, (Aeschulus Tragicus); σμικροῦ γένοιτ᾽ ἂν σπέρματος π. μέγας, i. e. great things might come from small, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

3645.full: 1. a leaf , mostly in plural, (Homer):—; poetry, νεικέων πέταλα contentious votes (compare πεταλισμός); (Pindar) 2. a leaf of metal , (Lucian) (ML)

3648.lxx: in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23
3648.full: στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT (στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23 ;] used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luk.3:14, 1Co.9:7, 2Ti.2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2Co.10:3, 1Ti.1:18, Jas.4:1, 1Pe.2:11.† (AS)

3649.full: στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jhn.6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (see B1., 9, 1), [in LXX: Dan LXX 4:9, Sus 1:37, 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:9 ff. * ;] a stadium, i.e. __1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mat.14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Luk.24:13, Jhn.6:19 11:18, Rev.14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course, __2. a race-course: 1Co.9:24.† (AS)

3650.full: 1. to moan, sigh, groan , (Homer) 2. with genitive to moan or sigh for , (Euripides); ὑπέρ τινος (Aeschulus Tragicus); τινί or ἐπί τινι (Euripides); with accusative cognate, πένθος οἰκεῖον στ. (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Mid., (Aeschulus Tragicus) 3. with accusative to bewail, lament , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; στένειν τινὰ τῆς τύχης to pity him for his ill fortune, (Aeschulus Tragicus): so in Mid., στένεσθαί τινα (Euripides) (ML)

3652.full: συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ [in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;] the mulberry tree (Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *), the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) † (AS)

3654.full: συν-θλάω, -ῶ [in LXX for מָחַץ etc. ;] to crush together, crush: Mat.21:44 ([WH], R, mg., om.), Luk.20:18.† (AS)

s: to combine in one city, unite under a capital
3655.full: 1. to make to live with , (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give him one's daughter in marriage , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to combine in one city, unite under a capital or metropolis , ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed , opposite to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, (Thucydides) 3. to join in peopling or colonising a country, (Euripides) 4. generally to unite, associate , (Plutarch) (ML)

3656.full: συν-οράω, see: συνεῖδον. συν-εῖδον irreg. aorist of συνοράω (see: εἶδον), [in LXX: 1Ma.4:21 א, 2Ma.2:24 2Mac 4:4 2Mac 4:41 R 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 7:4 2Mac 7:20 2Mac 8:8, 3Ma.2:8 A * ;] __1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.). __2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand (LXX, Polyb., Plut., al.) : Act.12:12 14:6 (on the related σύνοιδα, see see word).† (AS)

3657.full: συν-τέμνω [in LXX chiefly for חָרַץ ;] __1. to cut in pieces. __2. to cut down, cut short: metapb., λόγον, Rom.9:28 (LXX) (Hdt., Plat., Fur., al.).† (AS)

3660.full: 1. a hammer , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a beetle, mallet , for breaking clods of earth, (Hesiod) (ML)

3661.full: 1. a raft, float (such as was made off-hand , compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship , (Euripides) 2. a bridge of boats , of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

3662.full: 1. initiation in the mysteries, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐς χεῖρας ἄγεσθαι τὴν τελετήν to take in hand the matter of initiation , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural mystic rites at initiation , (Euripides), etc. 2. a festival accompanied by such rites , in plural, (Pindar); in singular, (Euripides) (ML)

3663.full: 1. far-shining, far-beaming , (Homeric Hymns) 2. of distant objects, far-seen, conspicuous , (Theognis Elegiacus) 3. adverb -γῶς, clearly, distinctly , (New Testament) (ML)

3664.full: 1. to shoot with the bow , τινός at a mark, (Iliad by Homer); εἴς τινα (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically to aim at , with genitive, (Euripides):—;absolute to use the bow , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; καθ᾽ ὑπερβολὰν τοξεύσας having shot too high, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. with accusative to shoot or hit with an arrow , τινά (Euripides):—;Pass. to be struck by an arrow , (Thucydides) 3. with accusative rei, to shoot from a bow : metaphorically, to discharge, send forth , ὕμνους (Pindar); ταῦτα ἐτόξευσεν μάτην hath shot these arrows in vain, (Euripides): —;Pass., πᾶν τετόξευται βέλος (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

3665.full: worked in relief : metaphorically elaborate , [variant datesAnthology Palantina from τορεύω (ML)

3671.lxx: in LXX: Exo.9:24 (לָקַח hith.), Num.21:14 (†), Psa.97:3 (לָהַט pi.), Da TH Dan.3:27(94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 *
3671.full: φλογίζω (φλόξ), [in LXX: Exo.9:24 (לָקַח hith.), Num.21:14 (†), Psa.97:3 (לָהַט pi.), Da TH Dan.3:27(94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 * ;] to set on fire, burn, burn up: figuratively, Jas.3:6 (on the meaning of the sentence, see Hort, in l).† (AS)

3673.full: φρουρέω, -ῶ (φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Est.4:56, Jdth.3:6, Wis.17:16, 1Ma.11:3 * ;] to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: 2Co.11:32; metaphorically, Gal.3:23, Php.4:7, 1Pe.1:5.† (AS)

3676.full: φωτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (φωτίζω) [in LXX: Job.3:9, Psa.27:1 44:3 78:14 139:11 (אוֹר), Psa.89:8 (מָאוֹר) * ;] illumination, light: metaphorically, 1Co.4:4 4:6.† (AS)

3677.full: 1. to mix something dry with something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive, χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have one's hair defiled with earth, (Pindar) 3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους from a confused and savage state, (Euripides) 4. in Pass. also to mix with others, have dealings with him, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

3678.full: χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;] a bridle: Jas.3:3, Rev.14:20.† (AS)

s: the foam that gathers at the edge
the first down on the chin
3680.full: 1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. the first down on the chin of youths, Lat. lanugo, (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom on fruit, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

s: to take part in the chorus
to be one of a chorus
3681.full: 1. to dance a round or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to him, in his honour , (Euripides) 2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically to practise a thing, be versed in it, (Plato Philosophus) 4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) 6. Causal, to set one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

3682.full: 1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

3684.full: a proposition carried by vote : especially a measure passed in the ἐκκλησία, a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ. νικᾶν to carry it , (Aeschines Orator); ψ. καθαιρεῖν to rescind it , Lat. abrogare, (Thucydides) (ML)

3685.full: 1. the bend of the arm, the elbow , (Homer) 2. generally the arm , like ἀγκάλη, (Pindar) 3. any bend , as the jutting angle of a wall, (Iliad by Homer): the bend or reach of a river, (Herdotus Historicus); ἕσπεροι ἄγκωνες, in (Sophocles Tragicus), seem to be the angle of the bay of Rhoeteium. (ML)

3686.full: ἀγνόημα, -τός, τό (ἀγνοέω), [in LXX: Gen.43:12 (מִשְׁגֶּה), Tob.3:3, Jdth.5:20, Sir.23:2 51:19, 1Ma.13:39 * ;] a sin of ignorance (so in π.; see MM, VGT, see word): Heb.9:7.† (AS)

3687.full: ἀγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἄγω), [in LXX: Est.2:20 10:3, 2Ma.4:16 6:8 11:24, 3Ma.4:10 * ;] __1. a carrying away. __2. a leading, guiding; metaphorically, training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life: 2Ti.3:10 (Cremer, 61; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

3688.full: ἀδελφότης, -ητος, ἡ (ἀδελφός), [in LXX: 1Ma.12:10,17, 4Mac .5 * ;] __1. abstract, brotherhood, brotherly affection (LXX). __2. Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community: 1Pe.2:17 5:9 (MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

3689.full: ἀδιαλείπτως (see supr.), adv., [in LXX: 1Ma.12:11, II Mac .4, 3Ma.6:33 * ;] unremittingly, incessantly: Rom.1:9, 1Th.1:3 2:13 5:17.† (AS)

3690.full: 1. a point, edge : proverbial, ἐπὶ ξυροῦ ἀκμῆς on the rasor's edge (see. ξυρόν); ἀμφιδέξιοι ἀκμαί the fingers of both hands, (Sophocles Tragicus); ποδοῖν ἀκμαί the toes, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the highest point of anything, the bloom, flower, prime , of man's age, Lat. flos aetatis, ἀκμὴ ἥβης (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμὴ βίου (Xenophon Historicus); ἐν ἀκμῆι εἶναι = ἀκμάζειν, (Plato Philosophus); ἀκμὴν ἔχειν, of corn, to be ripe, (Thucydides); also of time, ἀ. ἦρος the spring- prime , (Pindar); ἀ. θέρους mid -summer, (Xenophon Historicus); ἀ. τῆς δόξης (Thucydides); periphrastic like βία, ἀκμὴ Θησειδᾶν (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. like καιρός, the best, most fitting time , [variant datesTragica Adespota; ἔργων, λόγων ἀκμή the time for doing, speaking, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἀκμή ἐστι, with infinitive, 'tis high time to do, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐπ᾽ ἀκμῆς εἶναι, with infinitive, to be on the point of doing, (Euripides); ἐπ᾽ αὐτὴν ἥκει τὴν ἀκμήν 'tis come to the critical time , (Demosthenes Orator) 4. ἀκμήν, accusative of ἀκμή, used as adverb, just , (Xenophon Historicus) 5. yet, still , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

3692.full: 1. dimly seen, dim, faint, baffling sight , εἴδωλον ἀμ. a shadowy spectre, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. having no light, darksome , νύξ (Lucian):—; blind, sightless , (Sophocles Tragicus); so, ἀμαυρῶι κώλωι with blind foot, said of a blind man, (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. metaphorically, 4. dim, obscure, uncertain , κληδών (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐλπίς (Plutarch) 5. obscure, unknown , (Hesiod) 6. gloomy, troubled , φρήν (Aeschulus Tragicus) 7. active enfeebling , νοῦσος [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

3695.full: 1. to push back, stop short, check , ἵππον χαλινῶι (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid., ἀνακρούεσθαι πρύμνην to put one's ship astern, by backing water, (Aristophanes Comicus); so ἀνακρούεσθαι alone, (Thucydides); also, ἐπὶ πρύμνην ἀν., (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically to put back , (Plato Philosophus) 3. in Music, to strike up , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

3696.full: ἀνα-πηδάω, -ῶ (πηδάω, to leap), [in LXX: 1Ki.20:34 (קוּם) 1Ki.25:10, Est.5:1, To.4 * ;] to leap up: Mrk.10:50 (Rec. ἀναστάς) (AS)

s: to bring to light, make to appear
3697.lxx: in LXX for צָדַק hi., גָּלַשׁ
3697.full: ἀνα-φαίνομαι [in LXX for צָדַק hi., גָּלַשׁ ;] to bring to light, make to appear: ἀναφάναντες τ. Κύπρον, i.e. having sighted C.: Act.21:3 WH; pass., to appear, be made manifest: Luk.19:11 (AS)

3698.lxx: in LXX: Deu.19:10, 13 21:8-9 (נָקִי), Dan LXX TH Sus1:62, always of αἷμα (of. MM, VGT, see word)*
3698.full: ἀν-αίτιος, -ον (αἰτία), [in LXX: Deu.19:10, 13 21:8-9 (נָקִי), Dan LXX TH Sus1:62, always of αἷμα (of. MM, VGT, see word)* ;] guiltless, innocent: Mat.12:5, 7.† (AS)

3699.full: with the face towards, facing , τινι (Xenophon Historicus): face to face , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
